A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iP-VAE research, despite v2's retitling and expansion to FOND. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, sparsity, classification, and out-of-distribution experiments, including Table 1 and Figures 2–6.

after.justification: v2 retains original OOD results and adds model-family comparisons, MNIST results in Table 2, and simulated neural responses to drifting gratings in Figure 8.

M1.justification: v2 expands the proposed method family through FOND, introducing iG-VAE and iG-phi-VAE, including Gaussian parameter dynamics and post-sampling nonlinearities such as ReLU. The core online Poisson update remains recognizable in both versions' Equation 8; the new Gaussian procedures establish substantive method expansion.

E1.justification: The principal datasets remain van Hateren, MNIST, EMNIST, Omniglot, and ImageNet32, including rotated-MNIST testing. v2 adds a bounded synthetic test scenario: drifting gratings at four contrast levels to assess simulated neuronal response latency (Appendix C.3, Figure 8).

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated G-VAE and rectified-Gaussian controls, plus PC and incremental PC comparisons on MNIST (Table 2). The natural-image comparison also changes membership: v1 Table 1 includes ia-VAE(s) and sa-VAE, whereas v2 Figure 4 uses the expanded Gaussian/Poisson families with LCA. Hybrid baselines remain in the OOD experiments.

E3.justification: The main natural-image evaluation shifts from v1's MSE/lifetime-sparsity reporting to R2 and distance from an ideal reconstruction-sparsity point, retaining zero-fraction sparsity. v2 introduces systematic beta/training-horizon sweeps, an explicit convergence-detection procedure, deterministic posterior-parameter decoding, and model-specific MNIST training horizons of 128, 64, and 32 iterations.

E4.justification: Beyond retained rotation and cross-domain tests, v2 adds analyses isolating latent distribution and rectification, comparisons of sampled versus posterior-parameter decoding (Figure 9), systematic beta and training-horizon sensitivity (Figure 10, Appendix C.5.1), and cortical-response analyses (Appendix C.3). These address substantially more robustness and mechanism questions.

E5.justification: v1 Table 1 reports means and standard deviations without specifying random initializations. v2 Table 2 introduces 99% confidence intervals estimated from five random initializations, and Figure 8 reports 500-trial means with standard deviations. However, Figure 13's new description of standard-deviation shading does not match its retained bar chart.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the original natural-image performance table with expanded reconstruction-sparsity results and adds convergence, contrast-response, and MNIST findings. Table 2 reports iP-VAE per-dimension MSE of 4.39×10^-3 with 84% zeros, while P-VAE leads classification at 97.89%. These are new comparisons under revised settings; the original OOD findings largely persist.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix B.4 heuristically removes a rate-dependent gradient factor. v2 introduces Fisher-information derivations, natural-gradient dynamics, and a rolling-prior explanation for the disappearing KL contribution, plus Gaussian extensions. The new Gaussian derivation contains an inconsistency: Equation 44 omits the exp(xi) factor required by Equation 43, and subsequent update equations retain this omission.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from deriving iP-VAE under Poisson assumptions to FOND as a general framework producing several iterative VAE architectures. v2 additionally foregrounds emergent normalization, cortical-response properties, and systematic reconstruction-sparsity advantages across model families, substantially broadening the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations involving divisive normalization, exponential nonlinearities, and effective stochastic depth. It substantially extends v1's limitations discussion by acknowledging computational costs, biologically implausible training, architectural confounds in PCN comparisons, and the absence of direct neural-data validation (Appendices C.5.2 and D.5).

D1.justification: Compared with v1's limited experimental details, v2 documents learned step sizes and likelihood variances, optimizer and annealing schedules, learning rates, batch sizes, epochs, baseline libraries, GPU hardware, and compute requirements (Appendix C.1). It also supplies access information for the work's code, data, and checkpoints, although v1's standalone inference pseudocode is removed.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the work around Khan and Rue's Bayesian Learning Rule and Jones et al.'s BONG, newly connecting FOND to natural-gradient inference. The expanded background and Appendix D.4 also develop extensive relationships to neural sampling and MCMC approaches, beyond v1's earlier positioning.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, extensively rewrites the introduction, theory, and discussion, and builds a much broader background exposition. The main experimental narrative now emphasizes natural-image model-family comparisons, while the original OOD material moves to Appendix C.6 within a substantially reorganized appendix structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds conceptual and model-taxonomy diagrams, reconstruction-sparsity landscapes, contrast-response plots, and new model-summary and MNIST tables. Original OOD plots are relocated into Figures 12–15, while v1 Figure 5 becomes a redesigned feature display with enlarged examples in v2 Figure 16. Layout and captions are extensively revised.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the Poisson derivation and adds valuable comparisons, uncertainty reporting, reproducibility details, and limitations. However, its new Gaussian derivation omits the exp(xi) factor required by the stated reparameterization (Equations 43–44), propagating the omission into dynamics central to the expanded method family. The PDFs do not establish whether this affects only the exposition or also the evaluated models. These substantive benefits and unresolved theoretical consequences prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
